sections.html:
Western Kentucky's Breckinridge County follows the Ohio River across 586 square miles, which makes it large and sparsely settled at 35.9 people per square mile. Hardinsburg is the largest city and the seat, joined by Cloverport and Irvington. About 21,503 people lived here in 2025, a 5.2 percent gain on the 2020 count.

Owners hold 81.4 percent of the housing units, and the middle value of an owner's home is $156,700. Rent in the middle is $733 a month. Monthly owner costs in the middle come to $1,210 with a mortgage and $377 without. Builders pulled only 14 permits for 2025, which leaves resale houses with little new competition.

Breckinridge keeps Central time, but Meade and Hardin counties to the east keep Eastern time. When a closing involves offices on both sides, confirm which clock each office uses.

The sheriff bills and collects, the PVA values property, and the county clerk takes over unpaid bills.

Breckinridge County tax offices
OfficeContactUse it for
Sheriff's Office, 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg270-756-2361, PO Box 127, weekdays eight to four CentralPaying and looking up the current bill
Property Valuation Administrator270-756-5154Assessments and homestead questions
County Clerk270-756-2246Past-due bills and payoff amounts

Bills are mailed in late October. If yours has not come by early November, ask the sheriff for a duplicate. Online lookup and payment run from November 1 through 4 p.m. Central on April 15, and postmarks count.

The sheriff's stages on the 2026 bills run like this:

  • November 1 to 30: face amount less 2%.
  • December 1 to 31: face amount.
  • January 1 to 31: face amount plus 5%.
  • February 1 to April 15: face amount plus 21%.
  • After April 15: pay at the County Clerk's office.

The sheriff cannot bend any of this, because statute and the Revenue Cabinet set the dates and percentages.

sections.h2: How paying a Breckinridge County bill works
sections.html:
Send the exact amount printed on the bill and nothing less. A short payment comes back in the mail, and the sheriff offers no installment plan. One payment can cover several bills at once.

  • Online: a processing fee of 1.5 percent, minimum $1.50, applies on the first $60, and 2.5 percent on anything over $60. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and eCheck work.
  • Mail or counter: a check or money order with the voucher.
  • Fire dues: a signed opt-out form has to accompany the payment, so owners opting out pay by mail or at the counter.

The cancelled check serves as your receipt. If you want a receipt for a mailed payment, enclose a stamped, addressed envelope.

sections.h2: Getting your bill and paying on time
sections.html:
Mailing wraps up in late October. If yours is missing in early November, ask the sheriff for a duplicate rather than waiting. Online lookup and payment open November 1 and stay open until 4 p.m. Central on April 15, so a seller who is away can still pay without a trip to Hardinsburg.

For an in-person visit, the office at 208 South Main Street is open weekdays from eight to four Central. Bring the voucher from the bill. Pay by check or money order, and write the parcel details on the check if you have more than one bill.

Pick your window from the stages above. November takes 2% off, December costs the plain amount, and every later month costs more until the County Clerk takes over.

sections.h2: Before you sign a listing agreement
sections.html:
Taxes touch a sale in a few places, and each one has a person to call. The PVA's number settles what the home is worth on paper. The sheriff settles whether this year's bill is current. The clerk settles anything older. A title company will look at all three before a closing, and it is easier to learn the answers yourself while there is still time to act.

If your valuation looks too high, remember the dispute window opens only in early May. A seller who waits until the house is under contract has usually missed the chance to change that year's number.

sections.h2: Taxes when a Breckinridge County house sells
sections.html:
The bill is made out to whoever owned on January 1. Selling after that date still leaves the bill in your name, and you pass it to the new owner. The closing agent usually allocates each side's portion on the settlement statement.

Two prorated checks will not be accepted. Either you or the buyer pays the whole bill, so ask the closing attorney who will carry the payment and whether a credit goes to the buyer.

sections.h2: How an owner disputes a valuation
sections.html:
The PVA values property as of January 1 and sends crews back to each parcel about every four years. When a new number looks wrong, book a conference with the PVA during the inspection period, which starts in early May and runs thirteen days.

A filing with the county clerk, who acts as clerk to the local appeals board, is allowed only after that conference. The board convenes roughly a month after inspection ends. Boards rule on paper, so bring photos, a repair bid, an appraisal or comparable sales. An appeal without them is denied.

If you are 65 or older, or classed as totally disabled, you may claim the homestead exemption on the house where you live, worth up to $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. Every exemption question goes to the PVA, and a heavy-feeling bill is a good reason to check on one first.

A bill is delinquent after April 15, or after the tax day set for that year, and extra penalties may apply. The sheriff lets it go and it reappears at the clerk's office as delinquent, with a lien on the property. One percent interest starts each month, clerk and county attorney commissions follow, and notices and advertising come before any sale.

The Department of Revenue posts each county's delinquent list online by June 1, and on a normal schedule a sale can fall between July 14 and August 28. A third party can buy a bill that reaches the sale list.

Anyone selling a house here with old tax owing should order the payoff before closing so the title company can pay it from the sale.

1. Call the sheriff at 270-756-2361 and ask whether the current bill is paid.
  2. Call the County Clerk at 270-756-2246 for any past-due bill and a payoff figure.
  3. Ask the PVA at 270-756-5154 whether an exemption is on file and whether the value has changed.
  4. Tell the closing attorney who will pay the full bill and whether the buyer gets a credit.
  5. Forward the bill to your lender if it pays from escrow.

faqs.q: What is the Breckinridge County sheriff's tax office address?
faqs.a: 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. Payments by mail go to PO Box 127, and the phone is 270-756-2361.

faqs.q: Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, starting November 1. A convenience fee applies, and the payment must equal the exact bill amount.

faqs.q: Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff accepts the full amount shown on the bill, though one payment can cover several bills.

faqs.q: When does the 21 percent penalty start in Breckinridge County?
faqs.a: On February 1, and it runs through April 15. After that the bill goes to the County Clerk as delinquent.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax on a Breckinridge County house I sold in June?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed. The closing agent usually prorates the year, but the sheriff still needs the whole bill paid at once.
